title: Private DR: air-gapped backup bundles + offline restore from mounted repository
author: Diego Santos
description: Context: Several on-prem / restricted-network Private deployments cannot rely on any object store endpoint (S3/GCS/Azure) during incident response, and some environments require a human-movable artifact (USB/secure share) that can be staged and validated offline. This PR adds an air-gapped-friendly backup target mode that produces a single local “bundle” on a mounted filesystem, and adds an offline restore path that reads from that mounted repository. It also tightens config validation so operators get actionable errors before we start taking locks / entering maintenance mode. What’s included: (1) New storage target `local_bundle` that writes backups to a local directory (typically a PVC mount or hostPath mount, depending on deployment policy). (2) Bundle format: metadata JSON + checksums + compressed artifacts and DB payloads, written as a directory and then optionally packaged as a `.tar.zst` for portability (configurable). (3) Offline restore: allow `rw-private-dr restore plan/execute` to read from a mounted repo path without any remote endpoints; supports selecting a backup by `--backup-id` or `--path`. (4) Safer validation: validate path existence/permissions, free space, and filename constraints; refuse to proceed if we detect a non-empty output directory without `--overwrite`. (5) Documentation updates in installer README for air-gapped flows; examples for running in k8s via a mounted PVC. Non-goals: This does not add a new managed “staging repo service”; it’s purely a local filesystem target. This also does not change encryption defaults for remote object stores (covered in previous work). Security notes: For `local_bundle` we support optional client-side encryption using an operator-provided key file path (mounted secret). We do not persist plaintext keys and we redact key paths from logs (only basename). If customer policy disallows any key material on the node, they can rely on full-disk encryption / encrypted filesystem at the mount layer and keep `client_side_encryption` disabled. Testing: Added unit coverage for bundle manifest + checksum validation, and an integration test that writes a bundle to a temp dir, then restores from that bundle and asserts expected artifacts. CI runs the new integration test in the installer pipeline. Rollout: Safe additive change; existing S3/minio targets unchanged. Operators can opt into the new target via config. Follow-ups: (a) surface “backup bundle size estimate” in `restore plan` output (ENG-4920), (b) improve docs with recommended mount sizing guidance + failure modes seen in SUP-18511 (ongoing).

rw-private-dr: implement offline restore reader + backup selection by path/id
config: validate local paths, permissions, overwrite semantics; improve error messages
security: redact key path logging; add checksum verification gate before restore
tests: integration test for bundle create -> verify -> restore (local)

notable_snippets: Example config (excerpt): backup: { target: local_bundle, local_bundle: { path: /var/lib/redwood/backups, package: tar_zst, client_side_encryption: { enabled: true, key_file: /etc/redwood/backup.key } } }

CLI usage: rw-private-dr backup create --config /etc/redwood/private.yaml --output /mnt/backup-repo ; rw-private-dr backup verify --path /mnt/backup-repo/rw-backup-2025-11-27T031500Z.tar.zst ; rw-private-dr restore plan --path /mnt/backup-repo/rw-backup-... --dry-run
Validation behavior: refuse to write into non-empty directory unless --overwrite; fail fast if path not writable or disk free < estimated_backup_size_bytes
conversation: Fatima Noor (review): We need this to work with the common customer pattern where /mnt/backup-repo is a read-only mount during restore drills (write happens on a different node). Does restore do any writes to the bundle path? If yes, we should avoid it.

Diego Santos (author): Good call. Restore previously created a temp marker next to the artifact; I removed that for local_bundle paths and now write any temp state under /var/lib/redwood/tmp (configurable) instead. Added a test where bundle path is chmod 0555 during restore.
Connor O'Brien (review): For packaging as tar.zst: can we ensure atomicity? I’m worried about partial bundles being picked up by operators (or automation) if interrupted.

Diego Santos (author): Implemented “write to staging dir + finalize rename” semantics for directory bundles. For packaged tar.zst we write to `<name>.partial` and only rename to final name after checksum manifest is written and fsync completes. Also updated verify to explicitly reject `.partial` files.
Hanae Suzuki (security review): Please confirm we don’t log key material or the full path to key file. Also: do we require the key file permissions to be restrictive (0400/0600)?

Diego Santos (author): Key material is never logged. We now log only `path.Base(key_file)` and a boolean “client_side_encryption_enabled”. Added permission checks: key_file must be owner-readable and not group/world-readable; we error with remediation text if too permissive.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Can `backup verify` run fully offline and catch the common size/permissions issues we saw in the last drill? Also please ensure exit codes are consistent (non-zero on any warning).

Diego Santos (author): `backup verify` is fully offline for local_bundle and checks: manifest present, checksums match, required components present (db + artifacts), and encryption header if enabled. Exit code is non-zero on any failed check. I kept “warnings” only for optional components (e.g., audit export config missing) but those remain exit 0; let me know if you want strict mode.
Sahana Iyer (CI): Integration test flakes on mac runners due to zstd availability. Suggest guarding tar.zst packaging in integration with a build tag or using the pure-Go encoder.

Diego Santos (author): Updated CI to run integration tests on linux only and added a unit test that exercises manifest semantics without zstd. Keeping system zstd dependency for now since our installer images already include it.
Connor O'Brien (follow-up): Please add release note blurb for Private release train and confirm this doesn’t break existing configs.
Diego Santos (author): Added release note entry to README section and confirmed schema is additive; existing targets unaffected. Config validation only tightens when `target=local_bundle`.
release_notes: Private DR: Added air-gapped backup bundles (`local_bundle`) and offline restore from a mounted repository path.
Improved preflight validation for local backup paths (permissions, free space, overwrite semantics).
